name: Financial Reporting & Regulatory Filing (XBRL / trace-to-source)
definition: Agents that draft, iXBRL-tag, reconcile and file periodic regulatory reports (10-K/10-Q, statutory) with audit-defensible trace-to-source, sitting beside the funded finance back-office cluster.
labor_tam: $100-200B [W] — narrow high-comp slice: SEC/statutory-reporting staff (controllers, SEC-reporting managers, XBRL specialists) + external filing-agent labor, advanced-economy-weighted. Confirmed at frozen band.
sw_tam: ~$2-4B disclosure-management SW-TAM, incumbent-dominated (Workiva ~$800M+ rev, DFIN, Toppan Merrill); agent-specific slice small and being absorbed by incumbents, not a standalone software pool yet.
key_players: Incumbents internalizing FAST in 2026: Workiva (disclosure-mgmt leader adding AI narrative-gen + XBRL), DFIN/Donnelley (AI-powered iXBRL tagging launched Jun 2026), Toppan Merrill; adjacent finance agents that could extend into filing: Basis, Ramp Accounting Agent, Digits; Focus Universal/Perfecular (micro-cap EDGARization+XBRL). No VC-backed pure-play regulatory-filing agent pinned — this is the white-space. No verified independent ARR.
htc_entry_point: Narrow — seed only if a pure-play trace-to-source / officer-certification-defensible filing agent emerges below Workiva/DFIN. But the incumbent-internalization falsifier the frozen hunt-list itself named is already triggering (DFIN AI-iXBRL Jun 2026, Workiva leading), so the window is closing. No investable pure-play pinned today.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: if no VC-backed pure-play regulatory-filing/XBRL agent raises a Series A >$100M valuation while DFIN/Workiva ship AI-iXBRL at scale, incumbent capture is confirmed and the verdict locks to incumbent. Conversely a funded independent owning >10% of new AI-assisted SEC filings reopens the startup wedge.
anti_consensus_note: The frozen HTC hunt-list ranked W1.5 a top-3 open hunting ground (officer-cert liability = 'moat not wall'). I partially disagree: 2026 evidence shows the incumbents (DFIN AI-iXBRL Jun 2026, Workiva) internalizing the exact certification-defensible workflow that was supposed to be the startup moat — the falsifier the hunt-list named is already firing. The window is narrower than the frozen board implies.

name: Structured Data Entry & Digital Back-Office
definition: Computer-use + RPA-successor agents executing high-volume structured data entry, form processing and screen-based back-office transactions across enterprise apps — the RPA replacement layer.
labor_tam: $300-500B [W] — mass-headcount global pool (data-entry clerks, back-office transaction processors). Confirmed at frozen band.
sw_tam: ~$6-10B: legacy RPA base (UiPath ~$1.5B rev, Automation Anywhere, Blue Prism) being disrupted/absorbed by computer-use-agent spend; the CUA layer is new SW spend riding on lab model APIs.
key_players: UiPath (Screen Agent #1 on OSWorld-Verified at 67.1%, powered by Claude Opus 4.5, Jan 2026), Automation Anywhere, Microsoft (Power Automate + computer use), with Anthropic/OpenAI computer-use APIs as the underlying engine. Displacement is real but RPA/CUA revenue is SW spend, not coupled labor capture — no clean displacement ARR pinned.
htc_entry_point: None material — incumbent RPA (UiPath) + Microsoft own enterprise distribution and model labs own the computer-use capability (L=4); D=2 leaves no durable startup moat. Vertical single-app CUA point-solutions are possible but thin and easily commoditized.
falsifiable_indicator: OSWorld 2.0 long-horizon (multi-app, real-world) best-system score: crosses ~50% by Q4 2027 (from ~20% in 2026) -> back-office displacement accelerates and coupled capture rises materially; stays <30% -> long-horizon multi-app reliability remains the binding gate and displacement stays confined to bounded single-app tasks.
anti_consensus_note: The frozen conviction cited an 'OSWorld ~20% gate.' That gate has bifurcated: single-task OSWorld-Verified hit 67.1% (UiPath Screen Agent / Opus 4.5, Jan 2026) while OSWorld 2.0 long-horizon stays ~20%. The 'computer use is ready / RPA is dead' consensus is overstated — bounded single-app tasks cleared, but the long-horizon multi-app reliability real back-office work needs is still the binding constraint. I refined H 1->2 to reflect the single-task break; net stays Compression, conviction Medium.

name: Services-Arbitrage: Outbound SDR + Collections/AR Outreach
definition: BPO/agency delivery-model re-cut where voice+workflow agents replace outsourced outbound sales-development (W3.2) and collections/AR-outreach (W3.7) labor, typically success-fee-priced.
labor_tam: $30-50B [W] — the outsourced/agency slice of SDR + collections/AR outreach. Confirmed at frozen band.
sw_tam: ~$3-6B: AR/collections automation (HighRadius, Paraglide) charging 5-15% success fees vs contingency agencies 25-50%, plus discredited AI-SDR tooling. Collections side is the durable half.
key_players: Collections/AR (durable half): HighRadius (AI collections, success-fee), Paraglide, various 5-15% success-fee AR agents undercutting 25-50% contingency agencies. SDR half (collapsed): 11x.ai (~$3M retained vs $10M claimed, 70-80% churn, fabricated ZoomInfo/Airtable logos), Artisan (75-90% churn), AiSDR — category reverted to human-first/hybrid, capture approx 0. SDR-side ARR discredited; collections side more real but early.
htc_entry_point: Seed/A only on the collections/AR-outreach half (success-fee pricing, clean success unit, FDCPA/TCPA-navigation moat, V effectively 5 on the collections side). Avoid the SDR half entirely (11x/Artisan collapse, capture approx 0). No clean anchor exists — underwrite retained revenue, not booked ACV.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: an AI-collections vendor demonstrates >$50M retained (not booked) revenue at <20% churn on success-fee pricing -> collections-arbitrage wedge is real and coupled capture is climbing; if the category mirrors the SDR collapse (churn >50%, revert to hybrid) -> SA.2 capture stays approx 0 on both halves and the track is a value trap.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus lumps all 'AI outbound/GTM agents' as a hot displacement category and >$2.7B of 2026 GTM-AI funding is pointed there. The SDR half already falsified that thesis (11x fake logos, 75-90% churn, reverted to human-first). The durable arbitrage is the unglamorous collections/AR side — regulated, success-fee, clean success unit — the opposite of where the money is flowing.

name: Services-Arbitrage: Knowledge-Work / KPO (consulting, research, analytics)
definition: Delivery-model re-cut of judgment-graded knowledge work (KPO/consulting/research/analytics offshored to India/Philippines) where AI collapses the analyst-hour billing model — the ~$125B KPO/knowledge-services revenue pool.
labor_tam: $125B [$] — KPO/knowledge-services market-revenue proxy (research, analytics, financial modelling, design engineering). Confirmed at frozen figure; note [$] = vendor-revenue proxy, NOT a wage bill, never summed with [W].
sw_tam: ~$5-10B emerging: enterprise knowledge/research agents + 'AI employee' platforms positioned against the analyst-hour model; hard to size cleanly and heavily agent-washed.
key_players: Incumbents repositioning under pressure: Accenture, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, WNS, EXL, Genpact (KPO/BPO). HFS Research declared labor arbitrage 'past its shelf life' (Apr 2026). AI challengers: assorted 'AI employee'/KPO-displacement startups (agent-washing risk high). No clean displacement ARR pinned — this is vendor-margin compression, not a nameable startup anchor.
htc_entry_point: Largely none — judgment-graded work (V=2) blocks clean coupled/outcome pricing, and D=4 incumbent client relationships (Accenture/TCS/Genpact) dominate; the disruption is incumbent-margin compression, not a seed wedge. Watch narrow vertical KPO point-solutions (equity research, contract/legal review, financial modelling) but underwrite hard against agent-washing (Builder.ai test).
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: audited guidance from a top-5 KPO/IT-services incumbent (TCS/Infosys/Accenture/Genpact/WNS) shows AI-driven revenue-per-employee up >20% AND headcount flat-to-down -> knowledge-work arbitrage genuinely compressing; if headcount keeps growing with revenue (India/Philippines still ADDED ~120k/~80k BPO jobs in 2025) -> the 'end of arbitrage' thesis is premature.
anti_consensus_note: HFS/industry consensus (Apr 2026) declared 'labor arbitrage dead.' I discount this: the same 2026 data shows India and the Philippines still ADDED BPO/KPO headcount (~120k/~80k in 2025), and judgment-graded knowledge work (V=2) is precisely where outcome-verifiability is weakest — the least-clean displacement in the map, not the cleanest. The disruption is real at the revenue-per-analyst margin but the 'arbitrage is over' headline runs about an order ahead of audited headcount.

name: Autonomous AI R&D Labs ('AI that builds AI')
definition: Labs automating frontier ML research itself — experiment design, training-run orchestration, algorithm discovery — with the denominator being the elite AI-researcher wage bill / net-new research capacity. NEW this cycle (derived from E3 watch-line).
labor_tam: ~$20-40B [L] — elite frontier AI-research wage bill (low tens of thousands of researchers globally at $450-500k+ base; US employs ~59% of elite researchers by top-conference pubs, China ~30k active). Mostly LATENT/net-new research-capacity expansion (Mirendil thesis: 'frontier R&D within reach of universities'), not a displaced wage bill. Derived fresh; near-null displacement denominator wrapped in [L] optionality.
sw_tam: ~$1-3B and mostly indirect: the labs themselves are pre-revenue frontier shops raising $100M-$2B seeds. The real SW-TAM is the picks-and-shovels floor — Prime Intellect ($100M+ ARR verified, RL post-training/sandboxes/eval), Thinking Machines Tinker.
key_players: Core Automation (Jerry Tworek, ex-OpenAI VP Research; $100M @ $1B, then eyeing $300-500M @ $4B target ~6 weeks post-launch, 2026 — target, not closed), Mirendil (ex-Anthropic Neyshabur/Mehta; $200M seed @ $1B, a16z/Kleiner Perkins/Nvidia, 2026), Thinking Machines Lab (Mira Murati; $2B seed @ $12B, Tinker product), Discovery Loop (Jeff Dean/Google, internal). ALL essentially pre-revenue — valuations are NOT revenue. Infra floor (accessible): Prime Intellect $100M+ ARR verified.
htc_entry_point: None as a lab — $100M-$2B seeds, ex-frontier-lab founders, L=5 lab-captured, pre-revenue at valuations detached from revenue. The only accessible surface is the infra floor (Prime Intellect-style RL/eval/sandbox picks-and-shovels), which lives in the SW-TAM ledger / W8, not in this track.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: does an AI-R&D-automation lab (Core Automation/Mirendil/TML) ship a system that autonomously produces a reproducible, peer-recognized frontier ML result (e.g., new SOTA algorithm) with disclosed human-hours <10% of baseline? Yes -> 'AI builds AI' is real (L stays 5, still uninvestable at seed/A); No / still research-assist -> category is over-valued frontier-lab speculation with valuations detached from delivered automation.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus and the froth (Core Automation $4B six weeks post-launch, Mirendil $1B seed, TML $12B) treat 'AI that builds AI' as the highest-value frontier. Two corrections: (1) as a LABOR-TAM track it is a near-null denominator — tiny elite headcount wrapped in [L] latent optionality; the dollars are valuation, not a captured wage bill. (2) It is the single most lab-captured cell in the map (L=5) — uninvestable at seed/A for an outside fund; the only accessible value is the infra floor. P1's call to keep it a W8 watch-line rather than a full track was correct; promoting it risks importing valuation-as-TAM.

name: Scientific / Materials R&D Automation (AI scientists + self-driving labs + EDA)
definition: Autonomous 'AI scientist' and self-driving-lab systems running closed-loop hypothesis->experiment->analysis cycles in physical/computational science (materials, chemistry, drug discovery, semiconductors/EDA); denominator = the domain R&D scientist/verification-engineer wage bill. NEW this cycle (derived from E3).
labor_tam: ~$100-200B [W] + large [L] discovery-expansion tail — displaceable R&D scientist / lab-technician / design-verification-engineer wage bill across materials, chemistry, pharma-discovery and EDA, advanced-economy-weighted; the [L] tail (discovery that was never staffed) is much larger and unpriceable. Derived fresh.
sw_tam: ~$3-8B emerging: agentic EDA (ChipAgents — Series A expanded to $134M, 6x ARR growth H1 2026, 120+ deployments, 50%+ design-cycle reduction; ARR LEVEL UNVERIFIED, only growth-rate + deployment count disclosed) + self-driving-lab platforms + AI-for-science compute.
key_players: EDA/semiconductor (strongest commercial signal): ChipAgents (Series A -> $134M, 6x ARR growth H1 2026, 120+ deployments; ARR level unverified) vs incumbents Synopsys/Cadence. Materials/chemistry: Periodic Labs ($300M seed, Fedus ex-OpenAI + Cubuk ex-DeepMind; superconductors + chip-thermal materials), Lila Sciences ($550M raised, $350M Series A Oct 2025, REPORTEDLY raising @ $8.5B — unconfirmed, Flagship/Nvidia). Drug discovery: Recursion, Arctoris, Isomorphic. Valuations >> revenue throughout; ChipAgents is the clearest commercial traction but ARR unverified.
htc_entry_point: The EDA/design-verification wedge is the most investable cell in the whole R&D cluster — coupled displacement of verification engineers, V=4, real ARR growth, below-incumbent (Synopsys/Cadence) — but ChipAgents is already at Series A $134M, so hunt adjacent verification/test/DV point-solutions at seed. Physical self-driving labs (Lila ~$8.5B reported, Periodic $300M) are capital-intensive, robotics/regulation-gated and largely inaccessible at seed.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: does ChipAgents (or an EDA-agent peer) disclose >$50M VERIFIED ARR with net design-verification-engineer headcount reductions at >=3 named semiconductor customers -> coupled EDA displacement is real and startup-ownable; if Synopsys/Cadence embed equivalent agentic verification as a platform feature and independents stall -> verdict flips to incumbent. Separately, if a self-driving lab (Lila/Periodic) delivers a commercialized, third-party-replicated novel material/superconductor -> the [L] discovery-expansion thesis validates.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus bundles all 'AI for science' into one hype basket at frontier-lab valuations (Lila reportedly $8.5B, Periodic $300M pre-product). I split the track: the COMPUTATIONAL VERIFICATION slice (EDA — ChipAgents 6x ARR growth, 120 deployments, coupled displacement of verification engineers, V=4) is a real, near-term, coupled, startup-ownable labor-displacement cell — the most investable in the R&D cluster. The PHYSICAL wet-lab DISCOVERY slice is capital-intensive, robotics-gated (P), regulation-gated (pharma R=5) and mostly [L] latent expansion whose valuations run an order ahead of replicated results. Treating them as one bet is the error: EDA is coupled-Compression-and-investable; physical discovery is [L]-Expansion-and-capital-intensive.

name: Management & Strategy Consulting
definition: AI agents automating the analytical/research core of strategy engagements (deck-building, market analysis, synthesis) — the associate/BA leverage layer of MBB and Big-4 advisory.
labor_tam: $500-800B (global advisory billings ~= consultant wage bill + leverage margin; narrow-def market ~$375-842B, broad ~$1.11T)
sw_tam: ~$2-5B addressable by external AI-strategy vendors, but most value is internalized by the firms (BCG ~25% of $14.4B rev is AI services ~= $3.6B; Accenture $2.7B GenAI rev FY25) — external startup SW-TAM is small and shrinking as MBB build captive platforms.
key_players: McKinsey (Lilli, 72% of 45k staff active; BA class cut ~20%), BCG (Gene platform automates 60-70% of standard analytical workflows; entry-level -15%, data-science +35%), Bain (OpenAI alliance), Accenture ($2.7B GenAI rev FY25, real; $5.9B GenAI bookings). No pinned EXTERNAL pure-play vendor — value is incumbent-internalized. McKinsey 'workforce ~60k incl. AI agents' = public remarks, directional not audited.
htc_entry_point: None — external capture ~=0. The productivity gain is captured INSIDE MBB/Big-4 via captive platforms (Lilli, Gene); a startup selling 'AI strategy' competes with the client's own tools and lacks the trust/relationship moat. Adjacent seed wedge only in narrow deliverable-automation (e.g., diligence/CIM automation) sold TO the firms, not around them.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: (a) does any external AI-strategy pure-play clear >$50M ARR from enterprise strategy work (not internal MBB tools)? If yes, external-capture-~=0 thesis flips. (b) Watch MBB aggregate consulting (non-AI-engineer) headcount in FY2026-27 reporting — BCG's grew in 2025 on AI-engineer tilt; if total advisory headcount turns down YoY, leverage-pyramid compression is confirmed.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'AI disrupts/kills MBB.' Anti-consensus: AI STRENGTHENS the incumbents — they are the fastest AI-services adopters and internalize the gain, re-tilting hiring from BAs to AI engineers. Displacement is real but confined to the junior pyramid (a W1.1b-style seniority-composition story) and accrues to the partners, not to any startup. This is an incumbent-capture track, not a disruption opportunity.

name: Marketing & Content Creation
definition: AI generation and agentic workflows for marketing copy, campaigns, social, and brand content — augmenting marketers while deflating commodity content-production labor at agencies and in-house teams.
labor_tam: $400-700B (global marketing/content/advertising labor wage bill)
sw_tam: ~$3-5B realized AI-content SW today (AI copywriting category ~$3.5B, ->~$8B by 2033); report-mill '$30B agentic marketing content layer' claim should be discounted. Real vendor ARR modest and in some cases DECLINING (Jasper).
key_players: Jasper (~$88M ARR, DOWN from ~$120M in 2023; val cut to ~$1.2-1.8B; GPT-wrapper unwind, founder exodus — single-source ARR, flag directional), Writer ($1.9B val, enterprise knowledge-graph + governance moat = the surviving niche), Copy.ai (380k+ users, many free), HubSpot (agentic marketing stack), Adobe/Canva (incumbent tool capture); frontier labs (ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude) are the L5 commoditizer.
htc_entry_point: None for horizontal copy (Jasper is the cautionary GPT-wrapper unwind — ARR contracting). Narrow durable wedge only in enterprise brand-governance/compliance (Writer, already past seed at $1.9B) or regulated/vertical content. Seed door effectively closed on horizontal content; frontier labs own the base layer free.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q2 2027: if Jasper ARR stabilizes/re-accelerates >$100M, wrapper-unwind thesis weakens; continued decline confirms frontier-lab commoditization. Watch WPP/Omnicom/Dentsu FY2026 aggregate headcount — already >=18k agency cuts in 18mo, WPP -1,000 more by end-2026 (to ~97,388); continued decline confirms coupled displacement at the production rung.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: marketing content is a huge greenfield AI-app TAM ($30B). Anti-consensus: horizontal content is the MOST lab-captured, least-defensible app category — Jasper's revenue is FALLING ($120M->$88M) while the category 'grows.' Durable value is not in generating copy (labs do it free) but in (a) enterprise governance/brand-safety (Writer) and (b) the coupled displacement of agency production labor (WPP-style cuts), which accrues to advertisers as savings, not to content-tool startups.

name: Enterprise Knowledge Research & Synthesis
definition: Permissions-aware AI search + agentic synthesis over enterprise data — surfacing, connecting, and drafting from an organization's own knowledge, augmenting every knowledge worker's research time.
labor_tam: $100-200B (time-slice of knowledge-worker research/synthesis labor across the enterprise; a soft denominator, not a clean occupation)
sw_tam: ~$10-20B addressable (enterprise AI search + agentic knowledge), with Glean's verified $300M ARR (May 2026, ~90% growth) as the anchor; Copilot/Gemini Enterprise are the bundle-threat competing for the same spend.
key_players: Glean ($300M ARR May 2026, up from $100M early-2025 and $200M Dec-2025; $7.2B val; F500 customers ~2x YoY; 85% of customers use across 5+ depts — VERIFIED, well-corroborated), Microsoft Copilot (incumbent bundle threat), Google Gemini Enterprise, Writer (adjacent), Sana/Dashworks (smaller).
htc_entry_point: Horizontal seat closed — Glean ($7.2B, $300M ARR) crowns it and Copilot/Gemini bundle-pressure the base. Seed wedge only in vertical/regulated knowledge synthesis (legal, pharma, financial research) or agentic-research workflows the horizontal graph underserves. No clean horizontal entry at seed/A.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2026: if Glean sustains >$400M ARR with NDR >120% despite Copilot bundling, the standalone knowledge-graph moat is confirmed (startup-viable). If growth decelerates below ~50% as Copilot/Gemini bundle in, incumbent-capture wins and the category is a feature, not a company.
anti_consensus_note: Directly against the FROZEN FILE'S OWN 'weakest basis / Med-down' flag (set on a single $7M seed in P2): Glean's verified $300M ARR in 15 months makes this the OPPOSITE of weak — one of the best-corroborated additive/Expansion enterprise-AI markets in the dataset. The live debate is not whether demand exists (it does) but whether the category survives Microsoft/Google bundling — a distribution question, not a demand question.

name: Design & Creative Production
definition: Generative + agentic design tooling (layout, imagery, brand assets, prototyping) that augments designers and deflates commodity production-design labor — dominated by incumbent creative platforms.
labor_tam: $400-700B (global design/creative-production labor wage bill)
sw_tam: ~$8B+ AI-design-tools category (2026, growing ~22%/yr), overwhelmingly embedded in incumbents: Canva ~$4B ARR (AI-infused), Figma ~$1.3B rev run-rate; image generation is lab/OSS-commoditized (Midjourney, Adobe Firefly).
key_players: Canva ($4B ARR end-2025, 265M MAU, $42B val, Magic Studio agentic suite — 'one of the world's most-used AI services'), Figma ($1.056B FY25 rev +41%, Q1'26 $333.4M +46%, $19.3B public, native AI design agent May 2026), Adobe (Firefly), Midjourney (image gen); new entrants (Krea/Recraft-class) 'making Canva/Figma nervous' but sub-scale.
htc_entry_point: None at horizontal design — Canva ($42B)/Figma ($19.3B public)/Adobe own distribution + brand and ship agentic AI natively; image gen is lab/OSS-commoditized. Seed wedge only in narrow verticals the incumbents underserve (regulated packaging, CAD-adjacent, 3D/motion). Consumer/prosumer design is a closed door.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2026: does ANY new AI-design entrant (Krea/Recraft/Magnific-class) reach >$50M ARR independent of Canva/Figma/Adobe distribution? If none does, incumbent-capture is confirmed. Watch freelance-design marketplace (Upwork/Fiverr) creative-gig volumes/rates — sustained decline = coupled deflation of commodity production design materializing.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'AI democratizes design -> big startup opportunity.' Anti-consensus: design is where INCUMBENTS have most decisively captured the AI wave by shipping it as a feature — Canva is already a top-5 global AI service. Startup TAM at the horizontal layer is near-zero; the real economic event is deflation of commodity production-design labor (stock, layout, basic assets), captured by the tool incumbents and their users, not by new entrants.

name: Program/Project Mgmt & Ops Coordination
definition: Agentic project/program management and operations coordination — planning, workload balancing, milestone/risk tracking, stakeholder reporting, and cross-tool orchestration — augmenting PMs and thinning the pure-coordinator rung.
labor_tam: $500-900B (global project/program managers, PMO, and ops-coordinator wage bill; diffuse time-slice denominator)
sw_tam: ~$10-15B (PM software ~$7-10B + emerging cross-tool orchestration), AI slice embedded in incumbent PM platforms; standalone orchestration-startup ARR largely unpinned/unverified.
key_players: Asana (Work Graph, AI teammates like 'campaign strategist'/'spec reviewer', AI Studio), Monday.com (7 pre-built PMO agents shipped 2026: planning/workload/milestone/risk/reporting, 24/7), ClickUp, Notion, Wrike (all incumbents embedding agents); cross-tool orchestration startups (Lindy, Gumloop, Relay.app, n8n) — no pinned ARR, flag unverified.
htc_entry_point: In-platform coordination is incumbent-captured (Asana/Monday PMO agents, D4 workflow moat) — no entry there. The open seed wedge is CROSS-TOOL orchestration running continuously without human intervention (the one part still 'wide open' per 2026 landscape) — Lindy/Gumloop/Relay-class at seed-A. Underwrite retained usage vs incumbent bundling; agent-washing risk high.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q2 2027: if a standalone cross-tool orchestration agent (Lindy/Gumloop/Relay-class) reaches >$30M ARR with >120% NDR, the orchestration wedge is real and startup-investable. If Asana/Monday absorb continuous cross-tool orchestration into their platforms first, incumbent-capture closes the door.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus frames PM/ops as a large autonomous-agent TAM. Anti-consensus: in-platform coordination is already incumbent-captured (Asana/Monday shipped PMO agents in 2026, D4 moat) — no seed wedge. The only durable opening is horizontal cross-tool orchestration, whose economics are unproven (agent-washing, pilot-to-production chasm). Most 'coordination labor' displaced is a diffuse time-slice across many roles, not a clean occupation — so coupled displacement is real but slow and hard to capture.

name: Sales Closing & Account Mgmt (B2B AE)
definition: AI copilots/agents assisting or executing the B2B account-executive motion — deal execution, CRM hygiene, forecasting, call coaching, follow-up — for closing and account management.
labor_tam: $0.8–1.2T [W] — B2B account-executive + account-management + field-sales comp; large, durable-seat pool. Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$8–12B sales-AI/revenue-intelligence software 2026 (rev-intel ~$3.8B'24→$5.4B'28; AI-in-sales $8.8B'25→$63.5B'32 @ ~33% CAGR). Real anchor: Gong ARR >$500M May'26 (+55% YoY). Overwhelmingly seat/copilot, not coupled.
key_players: Gong (ARR >$500M May'26, +55% YoY — strongest real rev), Clari (forecast roll-ups), Salesforce Agentforce (redefined ARR — haircut), HubSpot Breeze, Outreach, Clay, Apollo. 11x/Artisan (SDR-adjacent) collapsed (70–90% churn). All copilot/'suggestive' autonomy — humans still close.
htc_entry_point: none — additive copilot on durable AE seats (Expansion, not coupled capture); incumbent-captured (Gong >$500M ARR, Clari, Salesforce/HubSpot own the CRM graph). No seed wage-bill-displacement wedge.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: does any AI-AE vendor disclose commission-replacing OUTCOME pricing (≥20% of rev-intelligence ARR coupled to closed deals) AND US BLS sales-rep headcount turn flat-to-down? Both → flip to coupled/Compression. Absent → stays additive/Expansion (base case).
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'autonomous AI AE' replaces quota-carriers imminently. Disagree — closing is trust/relationship-gated (H=4, V=2), the SDR cohort already collapsed (11x 70–90% churn), AE is harder. Value is additive copilot (Expansion); the real money is Gong-style rev-intelligence riding durable seats, not seat elimination.

name: Recruiting & Talent Sourcing
definition: AI agents that source, screen, match, and engage job candidates 24/7, automating recruiter/sourcer tasks across open roles.
labor_tam: $0.15–0.25T [W] — in-house recruiter + agency-sourcer wage bill (global staffing labor). Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$3–6B recruiting-AI software 2026 (ATS + sourcing + screening). Juicebox tripled ARR since '25 A ($80M B @ $850M Mar'26, 5,000 customers). Recruiting-tech funding ~$208M over 11mo of '25.
key_players: Juicebox (verified-8 spine; $80M B @ $850M, tripled ARR, 24/7 sourcing agents, ~5× recruiter efficiency claims), Mercor (talent-match, ~$2B annualized rev UNVERIFIED, negotiating ~$20B — flag), HeyMilo/Alex (AI interview), SeekOut, HireVue; LinkedIn incumbent (graph moat).
htc_entry_point: Seed/A in white-space adjacent to Juicebox (already B @ $850M — too late): agency-recruiter displacement, high-volume/blue-collar sourcing, or outcome-priced placement, ≤$100M post. Underwrite retained ARR + a bias-audit compliance moat.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q2 2027: agency-staffing revenue (Recruit Holdings/Randstad guidance) shows >5% AI headwind, OR Juicebox next round confirms >120% NRR + per-hire outcome pricing → coupled compression real. Flat staffing + copilot-only pricing → augment.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: recruiting is easily fully-automated (high-volume screening). Disagree — the hiring-bias regulatory gate (R=3: EEOC, NYC Local 144 audits, EU AI Act high-risk hiring) throttles autonomous screening, and the D-moat is LinkedIn's graph, not the agent. Net Mixed: real sourcer-time compression, but durable compliance-gated human sign-off + incumbent data capture.

name: Tutoring & Instructional Delivery
definition: AI tutors delivering personalized instruction, homework help, and language/skill practice — augmenting or substituting human tutors and instructional delivery.
labor_tam: $0.15–0.25T [W] — private-tutor + instructional-delivery wage bill; global tutoring market ~$150–200B+, plus a very large latent [L] access gap. Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$3–6B AI-tutoring software 2026, consumer-heavy (Duolingo ~$1.2B rev/Max; Khan premium-AI ~$150M/yr; Speak unicorn). AI-edtech raised $4.2B in '25 (62% of edtech VC). Generic tutoring deflating toward free.
key_players: Khanmigo/Khan Academy (~$150M premium-AI/yr; 700K users but only 15% utilization — weak production signal), Duolingo Max (~$1.2B rev), Speak (language unicorn), MagicSchool (teacher tools), Synthesis/Sizzle. Free ChatGPT/Gemini tutoring = the L=4 deflation threat.
htc_entry_point: Mostly none — generic tutoring deflates to ~$0 vs free frontier chatbots (L=4 model-lab capture). Narrow seed carve only: outcome-accountable / assessment-integrated / district-distribution or workforce-certification tutoring with measured learning gains — never the tutor-agent itself.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q3 2027: a pure-AI tutor sustains >$100M ARR at <30% churn WITHOUT a distribution/curriculum/outcome moat (i.e., beats free ChatGPT) → deflation thesis wrong. Watch Duolingo Max attach rate + Khanmigo paid-conversion 2026–27 (today 15% utilization).
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: AI tutoring is the killer app with a giant TAM. Disagree on VALUE CAPTURE — generic tutoring is exactly what free frontier chatbots do best, so it deflates toward $0 (model-lab captures via bundled consumer subs); learning-outcome evidence is thin (Khanmigo 15% utilization). Access Expansion is real; startup capture is not. High adoption conviction ≠ high capture conviction — the frozen 'High' is on Expansion, not on investability.

name: Collections & AR Outreach
definition: AI agents automating accounts-receivable follow-up, dunning, payment reminders, and collections outreach (email/voice/text) across the order-to-cash cycle.
labor_tam: $50–90B [W] — collections + AR-clerk wage bill (BLS bill/account collectors ~200K US + global; chronically understaffed). Confirmed frozen.
sw_tam: ~$3–5B AR/order-to-cash automation software (HighRadius ~$300M ARR incumbent; AI-natives Daylit $110M raised, Monk $29M, Fazeshift $22M, Paraglide €4.2M). Early — no verified-8-scale ARR yet.
key_players: AI-natives: Daylit ($110M raised Sep'25; 3× collections on high-risk, 75% cost cut — production metrics), Monk ($25M A/$29M total; 40% DSO cut), Fazeshift ($22M, YC), Paraglide (€4.2M, Bessemer). Incumbents: HighRadius (~$300M ARR O2C), Billtrust, Versapay.
htc_entry_point: Seed/A investable — cleanest W3 coupled cell (V=5). AI-native AR/collections at $4–30M rounds, sub-$150M (Daylit/Monk/Fazeshift/Paraglide tier). Watch HighRadius/ERP internalization; underwrite retained ARR + DSO-outcome pricing (not bookings).
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: an AI-native AR vendor (Daylit/Monk tier) crosses ~$50M ARR at >120% NRR → wedge real; OR HighRadius/Billtrust/SAP-NetSuite ship native autonomous collections and AI-native ARR stalls → incumbent capture. Watch next-round retained ARR + DSO deltas.
anti_consensus_note: The sleeper. Consensus underweights collections (unglamorous) vs crowded CX/SDR — but it's a CLEANER coupled displacement: V=5 (cash collected is unambiguous), L=1 (not lab-captured), naturally outcome-priced, AR chronically understaffed, real production metrics (Daylit 3×, Monk 40% DSO). Risk is incumbent O2C (HighRadius) internalization + FDCPA cap on the consumer-voice-outreach slice, not capability. Best risk-adjusted W3 seed cell.

name: External Audit & Statutory Assurance
definition: AI agents performing the labor beneath a signed audit opinion — workpaper prep, sampling, tie-outs, controls testing and assurance evidence-gathering — under a licensed CPA/RA sign-off.
labor_tam: $150-250B [W] (global statutory-audit/assurance wage bill; Big-4 audit revenue ~$60-70B is the licensed-firm core)
sw_tam: ~$2-5B and growing (audit-automation/AI-audit software: Fieldguide, DataSnipper, MindBridge, Trullion, Caseware AI) vs a ~$200B audit-&-advisory services base
key_players: Fieldguide ($75M Series C from Goldman Feb-2026, $125M total, ~$700M val, used by half of top-100 US firms incl. Big-4 — ARR unverified); DataSnipper (~$1B val, Index/Insight — ARR unverified); MindBridge; Trullion; Caseware IDEA; Thomson Reuters (strategic). Big-4 each committing $1B+ to internal AI.
htc_entry_point: None/narrow — audit-workflow layer (Fieldguide) already at a $700M Series C and Big-4-captured; seed door effectively closed. Only adjacency: non-audit assurance (SOC 2 / ISO / mid-market internal audit) the Big-4 under-serve.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q2 2027, does a Big-4 firm disclose audit-hours-per-engagement down >=15% from an internal AI build, OR Fieldguide cross verified $100M ARR? Big-4 internalization first = capture stays incumbent-side (hostile TAM).
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'AI-audit startups disrupt the Big-4.' Reality: the Big-4 are buyer AND competitor (each $1B+ to internal AI); statutory sign-off (R=5) keeps the opinion+liability inside the licensed firm, so startups become firm-tools the Big-4 buy or clone (DataSnipper/Fieldguide pattern). Displacement is real; capture accrues to incumbents, not new entrants.

name: Consumer / Access-to-Justice Legal (UPL)
definition: AI delivering direct legal help to consumers and pro-se litigants (forms, advice, self-representation) for the ~80% of legal need that goes unmet — gated by unauthorized-practice-of-law (UPL) rules.
labor_tam: $100-200B [L] (latent/unmet consumer legal demand — the access-to-justice gap; not a paid wage bill)
sw_tam: ~$1-3B realized, mostly SMB/founder legal rather than pure consumer (LegalZoom AI, Hello Divorce, YC-W26 cohort); consumer info-need increasingly served free by frontier chatbots
key_players: General Legal, Arcline, LegalOS (all YC W26 — but B2B/SMB/immigration, not consumer); Hello Divorce; LegalZoom (AI); Upsolve (nonprofit, lost SCOTUS cert Mar-2026); DoNotPay (FTC-sanctioned cautionary). Revenue small/unverified.
htc_entry_point: None — UPL (R=5) caps monetization while free frontier chatbots already satisfy the info-need, so the [L] pool deflates rather than forms. Investable only on a regulatory-sandbox bet (Utah/Arizona-style) opening paid non-lawyer AI advice — a policy bet, not a product bet.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027, do >=3 additional US states establish sandboxes/rule changes explicitly permitting AI legal advice to consumers (beyond UT/AZ)? Track UPL reform, not product. Upsolve's Mar-2026 SCOTUS cert denial = gate still shut.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'AI democratizes legal access = huge TAM.' Reality: the [L] gap is real but uncapturable — UPL forbids paid AI advice and free LLMs serve the info-need, so the market deflates; the visible YC-W26 activity is B2B founder/SMB legal, NOT the consumer access-to-justice pool. Low conviction confirmed.

name: Autonomous / Device-Cleared Diagnosis
definition: FDA-cleared autonomous AI that renders a diagnosis with no physician in the loop and bills under its own CPT code (e.g., autonomous diabetic-retinopathy screening) — displacing the diagnosing clinician for defined, ground-truth-verifiable tasks.
labor_tam: $60-100B [W] (slice of the diagnostician wage bill — screening ophthalmology, radiology, pathology — addressable by autonomous cleared devices)
sw_tam: ~$1-3B realized; throttled to a handful of cleared indications and ~1-2 reimbursable autonomous CPT codes (92229)
key_players: Digital Diagnostics (LumineticsCore/IDx-DR — first FDA de-novo 2018, CPT 92229); Eyenuk (EyeArt); AEYE Health (AEYE-DS). Cardiac/pathology players (Cleerly, PathAI) mostly assistive, not autonomous. ARR modest/unverified.
htc_entry_point: Narrow/watch — capability and the FDA path are proven, but the binding gate is CPT reimbursement (only ~1-2 autonomous codes exist). Investable only where a new autonomous CPT code is imminent in a fresh specialty; underwrite the reimbursement path, not the model.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027, does CMS/AMA establish >=2 new autonomous-AI CPT codes beyond 92229 (e.g., autonomous skin/cardiac/mammography)? New codes = market unlocks; none = single-indication niche persists.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'AI reads all scans, radiologists obsolete.' Reality: 8 years after the first cleared autonomous device, still only ~1-2 reimbursable autonomous CPT codes — the wall is reimbursement + malpractice liability, not accuracy (V=5 already). Radiologist headcount is up, not down; the bottleneck is a multi-year CMS coding clock.

name: Specialized Statutory Attestation
definition: AI supporting narrow non-financial statutory attestation and assurance — ESG/sustainability (CSRD), regulatory-compliance certifications requiring a licensed sign-off — outside the financial-audit core.
labor_tam: $50-100B [W] and shrinking post-Omnibus (ESG-assurance slice materially de-rated)
sw_tam: ~$1-3B and de-rating (ESG reporting/assurance: Watershed, Persefoni, Novata, Workiva, Sweep) — demand cut by the Feb-2026 Omnibus
key_players: Watershed, Persefoni, Novata, Sweep, Greenly, Workiva (ESG reporting); Big-4/audit firms performing CSRD limited assurance. ARR de-rated post-Omnibus.
htc_entry_point: None — the addressable pool is contracting. EU Omnibus (published 26-Feb-2026) raised CSRD thresholds to >1,000 FTE + >EUR450M turnover (~80% fewer firms in scope) and removed the reasonable-assurance escalation. Avoid; the regulatory tailwind reversed.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027, is CSRD reasonable-assurance re-escalated or scope re-expanded (reversing the Feb-2026 Omnibus cut)? Absent that, the attestation pool keeps shrinking — a negative-catalyst track whose falsifier has already fired negative.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus (2024-25): 'CSRD mandates a huge new ESG-assurance market.' Reality: the EU reversed itself — the Feb-2026 Omnibus cut scope ~80% and capped assurance at 'limited,' so the projected market is contracting, not growing. Rare track where the falsifiable indicator has already fired against the bull case.

name: Pharmacy — Licensed Dispensing & Verification
definition: AI + robotics automating prescription dispensing, counting and the pharmacist's final verification check — gated by state licensure requiring a licensed pharmacist to sign off on the dispense.
labor_tam: $100B+ [W] (US pharmacist wage bill ~$60-70B, ~330k pharmacists, plus technicians and global)
sw_tam: ~$3-6B pharmacy-automation hardware+software, growing (Omnicell, BD/Parata, ScriptPro, McKesson APS incumbents; Queue emerging)
key_players: Queue ($18.6M total, emerged from stealth Jun-2026 as 'world's first fully autonomous pharmacy,' 60-sec fill across 250 meds — pre-scale revenue); Omnicell, BD/Parata, ScriptPro, McKesson (incumbent automation); Amazon Pharmacy. ~73% of hospitals now use verification tools.
htc_entry_point: Narrow — retail/community autonomous dispensing (Queue) is genuinely early and shortage-pulled (3-4k pharmacist-grad annual shortfall = deployment tailwind, minimal displacement backlash), but it is a robotics-capex + state-board licensure play. Hunt the verification-software / remote-pharmacist-oversight layer over the full-stack robot.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027, do >=3 states authorize remote-pharmacist or AI-final verification for retail dispensing (removing the on-site pharmacist sign-off)? Licensure change is the unlock; the robotics is ready.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus: 'pharmacists are safe (licensed, trusted).' Reality: the pharmacist SHORTAGE (not surplus) inverts displacement politics — automation is pulled in to fill vacancies with near-zero labor backlash (the eldercare/E6 pattern). The wall is state-board final-verification rules, which bend under shortage pressure — but it's a robotics-capex clock, so realized capture stays <2% near-term.

name: Piece-picking, packing & palletizing
definition: AI-vision + gripper robots that pick individual SKUs, pack orders, and palletize/depalletize in warehouses & fulfillment, replacing manual pick/pack line labor.
sw_tam: ~$3-8B (2026) robot+RaaS deployment for the pick/pack/palletize slice; report-mill piece-pick sizing $2.58B (2026)→$20.8B (2031) @51.8% CAGR (Mordor — direction only, distrust). Mostly hardware+RaaS, not pure SW.
key_players: Dexterity ($95M raise→$1.65B val 2026), RightHand Robotics ($66M cum, Series C), Ambi Robotics ($66.7M cum, ~51 staff), Symbotic (public, Walmart-anchored systems/palletizing), Pickle Robot (truck unload), Mujin; Covariant acqui-hired into Amazon 2024, Berkshire Grey into SoftBank. All ARR unverified — revenue is hardware-sale + RaaS, no disclosed recurring figures.
htc_entry_point: Horizontal pick layer past seed (Dexterity $1.65B; incumbents scaling). Seed only in vertical niches — mixed-case truck load/unload, mid-market 3PL palletizing — or the grasp-foundation-model/data layer. Underwrite deployed-fleet unit economics, not RaaS bookings; realized capture <2%.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: a leading pick vendor (Dexterity/RightHand/Ambi) disclosing >5,000 production arms in paid deployment with <18mo per-arm payback = capture compounding; fleets staying <2,000 arms on hardware-sale revenue = capture stuck <2%, track stays Mixed/too-slow.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus extrapolates e-comm + labor-shortage into a ~52% CAGR vertical takeoff; I hold capture <2% of the $0.6-0.9T pool because grasp diversity (P=4) still caps reliable autonomy at uniform SKUs — and the scaled deflation accrues to vertically-integrated operators (Amazon post-Covariant, Symbotic/Walmart) on their own balance sheet, not to an independent arm-vendor ARR line.

name: Structured visual QC & inspection
definition: AI computer-vision defect detection on production lines — pass/fail quality inspection in electronics, automotive, food, packaging and metals — replacing/augmenting manual visual QC inspectors.
sw_tam: ~$3-6B (2026) AI-inspection SW slice inside a ~$15-20B machine-vision market (incl. hardware), ~15-20% CAGR (report-mill, direction only). Vision foundation models commoditizing the core model layer from below.
key_players: Landing AI (LandingLens; ABB invested Sep-2025, integrating into robotics suite), Instrumental ($80M+ raised, electronics/ex-Apple), Elementary (VisionStream, 99.9% accuracy, 1B+ parts/yr), Averroes AI; incumbents Cognex & Keyence own the installed base. AI-native ARR unverified.
htc_entry_point: Largely closed — Cognex/Keyence incumbents + ABB-backed Landing AI + commoditizing vision FMs squeeze AI-natives into a feature. Seed only in high-value verticals (semiconductor, battery, pharma-vial inspection) where defect data + physics is a moat; otherwise none.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: an AI-native inspector (Landing AI/Elementary/Instrumental) crossing $100M verified ARR while displacing a Cognex/Keyence base at a major manufacturer = AI-natives unseating incumbents; if incumbents ship equivalent deep-learning and AI-natives stall <$50M ARR = the category is an incumbent feature.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus frames vision-QC as green-field AI opportunity; I read it as the most incumbent-owned cell in W5 — Cognex/Keyence have decades of installed base and now ship deep learning, while vision foundation models commoditize the model layer from below. The AI-native startup gets pinched between the two and value accrues as a feature, not a new labor-capture line — hence net Mixed/augment, not Compression.

name: Commercial floor cleaning (structured slice)
definition: Autonomous floor-scrubbing/sweeping robots for large structured commercial/industrial spaces (warehouses, airports, malls, hospitals), displacing/augmenting janitorial floor-care labor.
sw_tam: ~$3-5B (2026) cleaning-robot market, ~20% CAGR — hardware+RaaS dominated, thin SW slice (fleet mgmt). Chinese ASPs falling toward ~$8K/unit, compressing the hardware margin.
key_players: Avidbots ($107M+ cum, $70M Series C; Neo/Kas scrubbers), Gausium (China, ~$50M, Series D, price leader), Brain Corp (BrainOS platform powering Tennant/SoftBank Whiz), ICE Cobotics, Pudu; incumbents Tennant/Nilfisk. Revenue hardware+lease; ARR unverified, no fresh 2026 venture round surfaced.
htc_entry_point: None as a seed software bet — hardware commoditized (Gausium/Pudu driving ASPs to ~$8K), thin software moat (D=2), no 2026 round surfaced, <1.5% capture. Any edge is cross-vendor fleet-orchestration SW or verticalized cleaning-as-a-service, not the scrubber.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: a floor-care vendor reaching >50,000 deployed units with a recurring SW/RaaS line >30% of revenue = durable RaaS labor-capture emerging; units staying hardware-sale with sub-$10K ASPs and no SW attach = commoditized hardware race, ~0 startup value capture.
anti_consensus_note: Frozen conviction is High — but that reflects displacement CLARITY (mature HW does the job), not investability. This is W5's clearest 'capability-mature, value-uninvestable' cell: the robots work, but value has commoditized (Chinese ASPs, L=1, D=2) and accrues to facility-service buyers as opex savings. Treat W5.5 as proof-of-concept economics for physical labor-capture, not a place to deploy seed capital.

name: Structured construction & offsite prefab
definition: Robotic automation of structured/repeatable construction tasks — layout printing, bricklaying, rebar, and factory-based offsite/modular prefabrication — augmenting scarce skilled construction labor in controlled settings.
sw_tam: ~$1-4B (2026) construction-robotics + prefab-automation deployment, ~15% CAGR. Project-based revenue; prefab factory build-out is capital-heavy, robotics slice still small vs. the ~$150B+ modular-construction volume.
key_players: Dusty Robotics (FieldPrinter layout, 91M+ sq ft printed, ~$16.5M recent round), Monumental ($32M Series B 2026 Khosla-led, ~150-robot bricklaying fleet UK/EU), Built Robotics ($112M cum, excavator autonomy via Cat/Komatsu channel), Canvas (drywall), Toggle (rebar). ARR unverified; project-based revenue.
htc_entry_point: Investable at seed/A — genuinely startup-led and fragmented (Monumental $32M B, Dusty ~$16.5M, Built $112M cum), no incumbent lock, structural labor shortage = Expansion tailwind with low displacement backlash. Best edge: single-task layout/rebar/masonry robots with a BIM-data moat, or offsite-prefab-factory SW. Underwrite repeat-GC deployment cadence, not sq-ft PR.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: a structured-construction vendor (Dusty/Monumental/Built) on recurring multi-site GC contracts with >100 active robots and proven repeat-customer payback = wedge compounding; deployments staying pilot/one-off with fleets <200 and no repeat-GC contracts = still too-early.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus lumps this with too-early dexterous general construction (W6.2); I separate them — the STRUCTURED slice (layout, prefab, masonry in controlled settings) is investable now while general construction is a decade out. The labor shortage makes it Expansion not Compression (no displacement politics), and because it's startup-led with NO incumbent lock (unlike W5.2/W5.4/W5.5), it's the one W5 cell where seed capital can still own the category. The trap is conflating it with humanoid-construction hype.

name: Structured food/beverage production
definition: Robotic automation of structured food & beverage production — prepared-meal and meal-kit assembly, portioning, packaging and repetitive line tasks in food manufacturing — displacing manual food-production line labor.
sw_tam: ~$3-4B (2026) food-robotics deployment market, ~13% CAGR — hardware+RaaS; Chef's per-meal RaaS is the first credibly RECURRING (not one-time hardware) revenue structure in physical W5.
key_players: Chef Robotics (category anchor — $43.1M Series A 2026 led by Avataar, $65.6M total incl. equipment debt; 100M+ product servings, RaaS-per-meal, >12 facilities US/Canada/EU; ARR undisclosed), Hyphen, Nala Robotics, Cala; Miso Robotics (Flippy — QSR pivot/troubled). Chef revenue recurring but unverified.
htc_entry_point: Chef is the anchor at Series A — seed edge in adjacent structured food-manufacturing niches (bakery, protein portioning, beverage/co-packing) replicating Chef's RaaS-per-unit model. Genuinely startup-led, investable at seed/A in un-served verticals. Underwrite RaaS retention + per-unit payback (Chef's 100M-serving flywheel is the bar).
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: Chef (or a peer) crossing ~$50M recurring RaaS revenue across >30 production facilities with NRR >120% = durable food-production labor-capture; stalling <15 facilities on pilot/hardware revenue = capture stuck <1.5%, track stays too-slow.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus is scarred by Miso/Flippy's QSR flameout and writes off food robotics; I hold the winning wedge is BACK-of-house food MANUFACTURING (structured, high-volume, labor-scarce, RaaS-priced — Chef's 100M-serving flywheel), NOT consumer-facing QSR (Miso's grave). It's the first physical W5 track with credibly RECURRING revenue — that recurring RaaS structure, not the robot, is the moat.

name: Skilled Trades — MEP install & repair
definition: On-site mechanical/electrical/plumbing install, maintenance and repair by licensed tradespeople (electricians, HVAC techs, plumbers, pipefitters) in unstructured built environments.
labor_tam: $1.0–1.4T [W] (advanced-economy-weighted; 4x/5x/6x comp band applied — licensed-trade fully-loaded comp is high, so even ~0% realized capture is a large notional dollar line)
sw_tam: <$50M realized. No MEP-specific robot ARR; rides horizontal physical-AI foundation models (Physical Intelligence ~$5.6B val/π-series, Skild AI ~$14B val/$1.4B-C Skild Brain) none of which is MEP-deployed. Trades/FSM software (ServiceTitan etc.) is additive augmentation, excluded from coupling.
key_players: No pinned MEP-robotics vendor with ARR (zero corroborated). Horizontal foundation-model labs (Physical Intelligence, Skild AI, Figure) are the enabling layer but none does licensed trade work in production. All capability claims here are demo-stage, not deployment.
htc_entry_point: None — hardware/dexterity + licensing clock, not a seed-software question. P=5 unstructured × R=4 license/permit/inspection makes MEP among the LAST physical tracks to convert. Only investable adjacency is the hardware-decoupled data/teleop layer (CyberOrigin thesis, E6), not MEP directly.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: does any robot/humanoid log ≥1,000 billable, code-inspected MEP-trade hours in production (not pilot/demo)? If still zero, W6.1 stays too-early and Expansion-by-shortage, not displacement.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus lumps all trades into a near-term 'humanoids do everything' story. MEP is the opposite: R=4 licensed + P=5 unstructured = one of the last to convert. Net is Expansion (trades shortage / aging workforce fills unmet demand), not compression. The 4-6x comp band makes the notional pool huge while realized capture ≈0.

name: General Construction — unstructured
definition: On-site general construction labor in variable/unstructured conditions — framing, concrete, drywall, general labor — distinct from structured offsite prefab (W5.6).
labor_tam: $2.0–2.7T [W] (largest single physical pool; 4x/5x/6x comp band applied)
sw_tam: ~$50–150M realized, all narrow-task: Built Robotics (autonomous earthmoving RaaS), Monumental (masonry), Canvas (drywall finishing). General unstructured-site robot revenue ≈0. RaaS/capex, not agent-software ARR.
key_players: Built Robotics (earthmoving autonomy — real but narrow, capex/RaaS), Monumental (masonry), Canvas (drywall). No general-construction robot with ARR. Horizontal humanoid OEMs (Figure ~300 robots but automotive pilots, not construction) not on jobsites.
htc_entry_point: None — robotics timeline. Largest blocked pool ($2.0–2.7T) but no software wedge; narrow-task autonomy (earthmoving) is capex/RaaS, not seed software. Watch narrow point-solutions, don't underwrite general-construction labor capture this decade.
falsifiable_indicator: By end-2027: does autonomous/robotic construction labor exceed ~$500M realized RaaS revenue globally, or stay <$150M narrow-task? <$150M confirms too-early.
anti_consensus_note: The single largest physical wage bill is also the FARTHEST from capture — P=5 unstructured + variable outdoor sites. Realistic capture <0.1% through 2028. Consensus 'humanoids on jobsites by 2027' is timeline hype; the durable near-term value is narrow structured tasks (earthmoving), not general labor.

name: Personal Care & ADL assistance
definition: Hands-on assistance with activities of daily living (bathing, dressing, feeding, transfer, toileting, mobility) for elderly/disabled — home health aides, CNAs, personal-care aides.
labor_tam: $0.9–1.3T [W] paid (+ ~$11T informal/unpaid [L]); comp band applied — US aide comp is low so dollar-weighting understates headcount, but the informal [L] tail is the largest latent pool in the map
sw_tam: <$100M realized, and it is companionship/monitoring not ADL: ElliQ (Intuition Robotics — companion), assistive exoskeletons (Cyberdyne HAL). Physical ADL (transfer/feeding) displacement ≈0 in production.
key_players: ElliQ/Intuition Robotics (companion, not ADL), Cyberdyne (HAL exoskeleton, Japan), Panasonic/Japanese eldercare programs. No production physical-ADL robot. Japan/Korea shortage-mandate deployments (E6, METI/SoftBank) are the leading edge. ARR effectively zero.
htc_entry_point: Thesis-aligned watch (⚑robotics/E6): the investable layer is the hardware-decoupled embodied-care DATA/teleop/sim layer under the Japan/Korea inverted-social-license mandate (where CyberOrigin sits), NOT a direct ADL-robot bet. Direct ADL robots: none — P=5 intimate dexterity + R=4 liability are far off.
falsifiable_indicator: By 2027: does any robot perform a reimbursed/paid physical ADL task (transfer or feeding) in production eldercare at scale (>100 facilities)? If care robots remain companionship/monitoring only, physical ADL stays [L] optionality.
anti_consensus_note: Demographics make consensus treat eldercare as a near-term robot market. Reality: physical ADL is among the HARDEST (P=5 intimate dexterity, R=4 liability) — today's 'care robots' are companionship (ElliQ), not ADL. The real value is the $11T [L] shortage-fill + the data layer, and it is Expansion (augment scarce labor), not displacement.

name: Field Service & equipment repair
definition: On-site diagnosis, maintenance and repair of installed equipment (elevators, HVAC, industrial machinery, telecom, appliances) by field technicians. FSM dispatch/scheduling software is excluded from the coupled pool (additive augmentation).
labor_tam: $0.9–1.3T [W] (comp band applied; FSM software excluded)
sw_tam: FSM software ~$5–8B market (ADDITIVE, excluded from coupling — ServiceTitan ~$0.8B ARR augments techs). Field-service voice/coordination agents <$100M emerging. Physical repair automation ≈0.
key_players: ServiceTitan / Salesforce FSL (FSM software — additive, real ARR but not labor displacement). Voice/coordination agents for physical industries — HappyRobot ($150M C, NDR >150%, freight-adjacent) proves the seed wedge. Physical repair robots: none in production.
htc_entry_point: Seed — the field-service voice/coordination/dispatch-agent layer (W3.6 ∩ W6.4; HappyRobot analog) is investable and has real NDR. Physical repair is too-early/none. Enter the digital-coordination wedge, not the robot.
falsifiable_indicator: By 2027: does an autonomous field-service coordination/voice agent reach >$50M ARR with >130% NDR (HappyRobot-style)? That confirms the digital-coordination wedge; physical repair capture stays ≈0.
anti_consensus_note: The dollars in 'field service automation' get captured by coordination/dispatch AI (voice + scheduling), NOT physical-repair robots. Consensus conflates the two; near-term capture is the digital wedge (Mixed), while physical repair stays human for a decade (P=5).

name: Cleaning & janitorial — unstructured residual
definition: Unstructured commercial/residential cleaning beyond the structured floor-scrubbing slice (W5.5) — restrooms, detailing, clutter navigation, variable surfaces.
labor_tam: $0.5–0.75T [W] (residual net of W5.5 structured slice; comp band applied)
sw_tam: Structured floor-care RaaS ~$300–600M globally (Avidbots, Brain Corp-powered, SoftBank Whiz, Tennant) — but that is mostly W5.5 and already at <1.5% capture. Unstructured residual ≈0. Low-margin, commoditizing.
key_players: Avidbots, Brain Corp (autonomy stack licensed to OEMs), SoftBank Whiz, Tennant — all in the STRUCTURED floor slice (W5.5), <1.5% capture. No production unstructured (restroom/detailing) robot. D=2: low moat, commoditized.
htc_entry_point: None — D=2 low moat, RaaS economics. The mature part (structured floors) is already incumbent-owned at <1.5% capture and commoditizing (no venture return); the unstructured residual is genuinely hard hardware. Neither is a good seed bet.
falsifiable_indicator: By 2027: does an unstructured cleaning robot (restroom/detailing, not floor-scrubbing) reach production deployment beyond the structured slice? Absent that, the addressable part stays the commoditized floor slice.
anti_consensus_note: Conv=High is misleading. The 'solved' part (structured floors) is solved = commoditized low-margin RaaS at <1.5% capture — no venture upside. The unstructured residual is genuinely hard. Consensus 'cleaning is solved robotics' ignores that solved means uninvestable here.

name: Specialty-crop selective harvest
definition: Robotic selective harvesting of high-value specialty crops (berries, apples, tomatoes, grapes) requiring dexterous picking, delicate handling, and ripeness discrimination.
labor_tam: $0.4–0.7T [W] (comp band applied; seasonal ag labor, immigration-constrained supply)
sw_tam: Report-mill '$3.13B 2026 harvesting-robot market' (direction only, R7 discount). Realized deployed RaaS ~$30–80M — ag harvesting crossed ~1,000 deployed units for the first time in 2026, but that is ~10.8% of ag-robot deals and only ~1.5% of ag-robot capital.
key_players: Advanced Farm (apple/strawberry — acquired by John Deere), Tortuga AgTech, FFRobotics, Traptic. Ag-robotics funding steady ~$120–150M/yr (capital-starved). Deere is consolidating the winners; deployment tiny (~1,000 units). ARR unverified, mostly per-acre/RaaS pilots.
htc_entry_point: None for seed — capital-intensive, seasonal, crop-specific hardware; John Deere absorbs winners; thin venture-capital efficiency (1.5% of ag capital). Not an independent-returns market.
falsifiable_indicator: 2026 crossed ~1,000 deployed harvest units. Falsifier: does the deployed fleet exceed ~5,000 units / >$300M realized RaaS by end-2027 (genuine market formation), or stall near 2026 levels?
anti_consensus_note: Expansion (labor-shortage-driven) is right, but the '1,000 units in 2026' milestone is market-formation theater — seasonal, crop-specific, 1.5% of ag capital, and Deere acquires the winners. High Conv reflects clean verifiability (V=5, yield is measurable), not deployment scale or venture returns for independents.

name: Commercial food prep — QSR
definition: Commercial kitchen / quick-service-restaurant back-of-house food preparation — frying, grilling, assembly, beverage — QSR and prepared-meal production labor.
labor_tam: $0.6–0.9T [W] (comp band applied)
sw_tam: ~$50–150M realized. Chef Robotics food-assembly RaaS has genuine production (prepared-meal manufacturing, per-meal pricing). Sweetgreen Infinite Kitchen is chain capex. Miso Robotics (Flippy) stalled/downsized. QSR-storefront robot ARR small/unverified.
key_players: Chef Robotics (food-assembly RaaS — real production evidence, ~Series A), Sweetgreen Infinite Kitchen (chain-captive, deployed), Chipotle (Hyphen/autocado pilots), Nala Robotics. Miso Robotics (Flippy) — stalled, valuation cut. ARR unverified except Chef's per-meal traction.
htc_entry_point: Narrow — food-assembly RaaS (Chef Robotics, production-proven) is the one wedge with real deployment evidence, but Series A is done and unit economics are thin. Broader QSR-storefront is too-early / chain-captive (Sweetgreen, Chipotle build their own). Watch, don't chase.
falsifiable_indicator: By 2027: does robotic QSR/food prep exceed ~$100M realized RaaS revenue, OR do 2+ major chains standardize on a robotic prep line (Sweetgreen/Chipotle)? Storefront-robot stall (Miso pattern) = too-early confirmed.
anti_consensus_note: The real production evidence is in food MANUFACTURING assembly (Chef Robotics), not flashy QSR storefronts (Miso Flippy stalled). Consensus fixates on the storefront robot; the durable wedge is back-of-house prepared-meal assembly. Mixed net — chains build captive lines (Sweetgreen), squeezing independent RaaS.

name: Psychotherapy & Clinical Mental-Health Alliance
definition: AI delivering or supporting psychotherapy / clinical mental-health treatment — conversational therapeutic support, between-session coaching, triage — measured against the licensed-therapist relational alliance, the archetypal trust/relational-premium role.
labor_tam: ~$50B US / $100-130B global [W] (licensed-therapist wage bill: ~600k US therapists + counselors, ~$40-50B loaded US; global $100-130B). Confirmed vs frozen. Separately a large [L] access gap — US projected short ~200k mental-health counselors by 2037; global spend ~2% of health budgets — but that latent demand is unpaid and does not convert to a displaceable wage bill.
sw_tam: Small realized ARR, est. <$50-150M category and UNVERIFIED (consumer subscription, no company discloses therapy ARR). Slingshot/Ash $93M raised, Wysa ~$35M raised — raises, not revenue. Market-research 'digital mental health' multi-$B TAMs conflate human-therapist telehealth marketplaces (BetterHelp/Talkspace), not AI. The dominant actual 'AI therapy' usage is unpriced informal general-LLM (ChatGPT/Claude) use no startup monetizes.
key_players: Slingshot AI / Ash ($93M, a16z/Radical/Forerunner — no verified ARR); Wysa (~$35M total, clinical/employer channel); Sonia; Limbic (UK NHS triage — real deployment); Ash. Woebot wound down its consumer app 2025. Character.AI / companion bots implicated in wrongful-death suits driving the 2026 regulatory clampdown. General LLM labs (OpenAI/Anthropic) are the dominant informal substitute.
htc_entry_point: Direct-to-consumer AI therapist: NONE — 2026 regulatory wall (4 state bans as of Jul 2026), wrongful-death liability, and zero verified ARR. Investable wedge is the WOPR-carve-out lane: clinician-augmentation / administrative support (documentation, measurement-based care, intake/triage, between-session engagement) sold B2B to provider groups and payers, seed/A ~$10-30M post. Underwrite reimbursement path + clinical evidence, not consumer subs.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: BULL if a payer/health-system reimburses an autonomous AI-therapy product under a coverage/CPT code AND at least one state repeals or narrows its AI-therapy ban (the direct-to-consumer wall cracks). BEAR/base if US states banning AI therapy rise from 4 (Jul 2026) to >=8 with no reimbursement code — market stays clinician-augmentation only.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus chases the a16z 'AI therapist for everyone' story (Slingshot/Ash); the anti-consensus fact is that 2026 is the year the door SLAMMED — Illinois WOPR Act + NV/RI/ME outright bans, 70+ bills across 36 states, wrongful-death litigation. Therapy is the cleanest 'relational premium survives' case: the licensed human is legally protected and durable (Additive/Expansion), the DTC AI-therapist category is a regulatory/liability trap, and the largest real usage is unpriced informal ChatGPT use nobody captures.

name: Real-Estate Brokerage & Property Management
definition: AI agents running real-estate brokerage workflows (lead intake, listing creation, tour scheduling, transaction coordination) and property-management operations (leasing, resident/tenant communication, maintenance dispatch), against the agent-commission and PM-fee pools.
labor_tam: ~$100-200B commission/fee [$] proxy (confirmed). US residential agent-commission pool ~$100-115B (NAR ~1.2-1.45M members, avg commission ~5.7% on ~$1.8-2T sales volume) + property-management fee pool. Note this is a market-revenue proxy, not a clean wage bill.
sw_tam: Proptech AI, anchored by EliseAI ($2.2B val on $250M Series E, in talks at $3.7B; platform across ~10% of US apartments — implies material, though unverified, ARR likely $100M+). Brokerage-side lead-gen/CRM/transaction copilots are a fragmented, largely incumbent-portal-adjacent layer. 97% of brokerage leaders report active agent AI use (Jan 2026) — adoption, not displacement.
key_players: EliseAI (property-mgmt leasing/resident comms — the genuine displacement anchor, $2.2B→$3.7B val, ~10% of US apartment market); brokerage side: Compass (AI tools + Redfin coming-soon deal), Zillow (Preview launched Mar 2026, portal-data moat), Redfin; lead-intake/transaction copilots (Perspective AI, Bounti). NAR settlement is reshaping the commission structure (commissions rose, not fell).
htc_entry_point: The residential AGENT is durable/fiduciary — commission copilots are crowded and incumbent-portal-adjacent (avoid). The real coupled-displacement wedge is PROPERTY-MANAGEMENT ops (leasing, resident comms, maintenance), but the anchor (EliseAI) is late/expensive. Seed/A ~$15-40M in vertical PM-ops for underserved asset classes (SFR, commercial, HOA) or transaction-coordination automation where a vertical isn't yet owned.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: BULL if an EliseAI-class PM-ops AI is shown (audited, not vendor claim) to have cut >=20% of leasing/PM-admin headcount at a top-10 apartment operator — PM leasing is real coupled compression. BEAR if the residential commission pool stays flat-to-up (post-settlement ~5.7%) and agent headcount is stable — brokerage remains additive augmentation.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus frames 'the AI real-estate agent' as the disruption; the anti-consensus read is that the residential agent is one of the most durable relational/fiduciary roles (commissions went UP after the NAR settlement, not down), while the actual, quieter displacement is in property-management back-office — leasing and resident comms (EliseAI) — a different, less-glamorous pool. Brokerage = expansion/augment; PM ops = the real coupled compression, and the only place to hunt.

name: Agent Ops & Fleet Supervision
definition: Net-new HUMAN roles the agent economy creates to monitor, govern, and supervise deployed agent fleets — human-in-the-loop checkpoints, high-stakes-action approval, drift/hallucination escalation, rollback. The labor shadow of the AgentOps control-plane; priced as a net-new wage bill [W] (the software beneath is a parallel [$] SW-TAM entry).
labor_tam: ~$10-20B [W] net-new (frozen retained; LOW confidence — flag: this is an implied/emerging pool, the distinct 'agent supervisor' title barely exists in 2026 and is mostly folded into existing ops/platform/MLOps roles). MarketsandMarkets AI-agents $52.6B-by-2030 and similar are SOFTWARE TAMs, not the labor line — do not import.
sw_tam: AgentOps / agent-governance / observability control-plane, [$] parallel ledger (NEVER summed into the labor line). Incumbent-captured: Microsoft Agent 365 (~$15/user/mo), ServiceNow AI Control Tower, Salesforce, UiPath AgentOps; independent observability tail (AgentOps.ai, Braintrust-adjacent). Pure-play standalone ARR undisclosed/small.
key_players: Tooling (the [$] shadow): Microsoft Agent 365, ServiceNow AI Control Tower, Salesforce Agentforce ops, UiPath, AgentOps.ai. The HUMAN line is diffuse net-new headcount inside enterprises and BPOs (fleet-ops operators, agent supervisors) — no pure-play labor vendor; the role is nascent and not yet a distinct occupation.
htc_entry_point: Mostly NONE for the labor line (diffuse headcount, not a company) and the tooling beneath it is incumbent-captured (Agent 365 + Control Tower colonizing) — a hostile standalone SW-TAM. Narrow seed wedge: managed agent-supervision-as-a-service / BPO-delivered human-in-the-loop, or vertical observability/governance where the incumbent control-plane doesn't reach (regulated, on-prem, multi-vendor fleets).
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: BULL if 'Agent Operations Manager'/'agent supervisor' emerges as a distinct high-volume title (e.g. >=25k US postings) with its own comp band — a real net-new occupation. BEAR if the function stays absorbed into existing MLOps/ops roles, no distinct title emerges, and the control-plane is fully owned by Microsoft/ServiceNow — W8.1 is a feature, not a labor market.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus (and the AgentOps vendors) forecast a large new 'humans supervising agent fleets' workforce. Anti-consensus: the pool is real but small and structurally captured — the supervision tooling is being absorbed by the same incumbents that ship the agents (Agent 365, ServiceNow Control Tower), so it is neither a big labor pool nor an independent software opportunity. And as agent reliability rises, the agents-per-supervisor ratio rises, capping headcount — it self-shrinks as the tech improves.

name: Forward-Deployed Integration / FDE
definition: Net-new HUMAN forward-deployed engineers embedded with customers to integrate, configure, and productionize agents inside the customer's operational environment — the labor that bridges the pilot-to-production chasm. Priced as a net-new wage bill [W]; the strongest-corroborated labor-creation line in the map.
labor_tam: ~$10-18B [W] net-new (refined up from frozen $8-15B on the 2026 surge; direction is HIGH-conviction, dollar sizing is the softer part — flag: headcount is the binding uncertainty, comp anchors are solid). Comp well-anchored: Palantir FDSE median ~$211K (Levels.fyi), OpenAI/Anthropic $350-550K, 2026 median mid-level FDE ~$385K, staff ~$610K, principal ~$1.2M.
sw_tam: n/a as a track denominator — this is a pure labor line, not a software category. The relevant [$] adjacency is the internal-tools / agent-scaffolding / deployment tooling that leverages FDEs (small, fragmented).
key_players: OpenAI (launched the $4B 'OpenAI Deployment Company' subsidiary May 11 2026, built entirely around FDEs; acquired a ~150-FDE consulting firm to seed it), Anthropic, Google, Salesforce, Databricks, Palantir (originator), McKinsey QuantumBlack — all hiring FDE or equivalents. Reported ~800% YoY posting surge (report-mill figure, flagged; comp/hiring corroboration is solid).
htc_entry_point: The labor line isn't a direct equity buy. Investable proxies: (1) FDE-heavy AI-native implementation boutiques (Palantir-model applied to agents) — but services margins fit VC poorly; (2) FDE-PRODUCTIVITY tooling / agent-scaffolding / deployment platforms that give leverage over the labor. Seed/A. Discipline flag: underwrite the productized/tooling leverage layer, not the raw services headcount (services-margin trap). Raw labor pool = not directly investable.
falsifiable_indicator: By Q4 2027: BULL if 'Forward Deployed Engineer' sustains >=50k active postings AND OpenAI Deployment Company / equivalents scale past ~1,000 FDEs with disclosed revenue — durable net-new market. BEAR if, as agents self-deploy and reliability rises, FDE demand plateaus and re-absorbs into standard solutions-engineering — a transitional bridge, not a durable occupation. Resolver: does FDE headcount keep RISING as model reliability improves (chasm durable) or fall (chasm closes)?
anti_consensus_note: Consensus dismisses FDE as Palantir-nostalgia or a temporary bridge that shrinks as agents improve. Anti-consensus: it is the single clearest, best-corroborated net-new labor line in the map (OpenAI built a $4B subsidiary around it) precisely BECAUSE the pilot-to-production chasm is structural, not transitional — harder-pushed capability widens the deployment gap, so FDE demand is near-term counter-cyclical to model progress. Caveat: it's labor, not software — real value, hard to capture in a venture-scalable wrapper.

name: Agent Trust, Insurance & Audit
definition: Net-new HUMAN roles the agent economy creates to insure, certify, and audit agent behavior and liability — AI-liability underwriters, AI auditors, certification/assurance staff. Priced as a net-new wage bill [W]; a regulatory- and liability-driven accountability floor beneath deployed agents.
labor_tam: ~$2-5B [W] net-new (frozen retained; LOW confidence — embryonic. Only ~5 dedicated AI-liability insurance products exist worldwide as of early 2026; premiums tiny). The audit/assurance headcount could grow materially on EU AI Act conformity demand, but is not yet a sizable payroll line.
sw_tam: Straddles insurance capital + AI-risk-assessment IP. Standalone AI-liability products: Armilla (Lloyd's coverholder, up to $25M/org, 500+ AI evaluations), Munich Re aiSure (via Mosaic, up to $15M), Testudo (Lloyd's Lab, up to $9.25M). Feb 2026 Armilla+Chaucer 'Vanguard AI' bundles AI liability with cyber/tech-E&O — the tell that AI risk is being absorbed into existing lines, not spun standalone.
key_players: Armilla AI (Lloyd's/Chaucer-backed, MGA + AI certification, 500+ evals — the startup wedge); Munich Re aiSure (incumbent, since 2018); Testudo (Lloyd's Lab); Chaucer/Lloyd's (risk capital). Some insurers cover hallucinations, others explicitly exclude AI — the market is splitting in 2026.
htc_entry_point: The investable wedge is the MGA/coverholder + AI-certification model (Armilla): a startup owns AI-risk-underwriting IP and a proprietary loss/eval data flywheel while incumbent Lloyd's/reinsurer capital carries balance-sheet risk. Seed/A ~$10-30M. Adjacent: AI-audit/assurance-as-a-service tied to EU AI Act conformity. Flag: very early (Low conviction), premiums tiny; the audit-labor line itself isn't directly investable — underwrite the data moat, not the premium.
falsifiable_indicator: By 2027 (as insurers accumulate loss data + EU AI Act GPAI enforcement bites): BULL if standalone AI-liability premium written globally crosses ~$500M AND a startup MGA (Armilla-class) builds a durable loss-ratio-backed book — a real net-new market with a startup wedge. BEAR if AI risk keeps getting absorbed into cyber/tech-E&O (the 'Vanguard AI' bundling pattern generalizes) and dedicated AI insurers stay sub-scale — a rider on existing lines, not a category.
anti_consensus_note: Consensus is bimodal — AI-insurance boosters ('a new multi-billion category') vs skeptics ('insurers will just exclude AI'). Anti-consensus: the tell is Chaucer's 'Vanguard AI' bundle — AI risk is being absorbed into cyber/E&O, not spun into a standalone line, capping the pure-play. The durable startup wedge is NOT the insurance capital (incumbent Lloyd's/Munich Re) but the AI-risk-assessment/certification data moat (Armilla's 500+ evals become actuarial gold). It's also a leading indicator — dedicated AI insurance only scales once real agent-failure losses hit balance sheets; today it prices tail risk blind.

name: Rideshare, Taxi & Robotaxi
definition: Human rideshare/taxi/for-hire drivers displaced by autonomous robotaxi fleets on dense urban route networks.
labor_tam: $0.3-0.5T [W] confirmed (US-weighted for-hire driver wage bill; low comp-per-head, dollar-weighting de-emphasizes vs headcount).
sw_tam: ~$0.5-1.5B global robotaxi ride/service revenue 2026 ([$] proxy, not labor capture): Waymo ~$355M annualized (Feb-26) tracking toward ~$1B at 1M weekly rides; Baidu Apollo Go 100M+ cumulative rides; Pony robotaxi rev only $12.1M in Q2-26 (+691% off tiny base).
key_players: Waymo (Alphabet, ~500-713K weekly rides 2026, 5+ new metros); Tesla robotaxi (~700K paid miles since Jun-25, still partly supervised, 7-city H1-26 push — discount Musk 'widespread by EOY26'); Baidu Apollo Go; Pony.ai (fleet target 3,500, ~1,975 live); WeRide; Zoox (Amazon). Realized capture <1% of driver pool.
htc_entry_point: None at the vehicle layer — capex-in-the-billions, big-tech/OEM captured (Alphabet, Tesla, Amazon, Baidu). Adjacent seed surface = AV remote-operations/teleop, safety-case/simulation data, and fleet-ops software feeding the crowned stacks.
falsifiable_indicator: Does Waymo hit its stated 1M weekly paid rides (~$1B annualized) by Q4-2026? Q4-26 median forecasts sit ~713K, short of target; a miss confirms the multi-year capex-grind read. Also watch any US metro posting measurable net taxi/rideshare-driver headcount decline in BLS/city data by mid-2027.
anti_consensus_note: Tesla-bull consensus treats 'widespread driverless 2026' as imminent mass displacement. Even the leader (Waymo) is ~$355M annualized on <0.5% capture, net driver headcount is still RISING (gig growth), and this is a decade capex grind not a 2026 event. Apply the Unitree rule: never convert robotaxi valuations or ride-count headlines into deployed labor displacement.

name: Long-haul & Regional Trucking
definition: Long-haul/regional truck drivers displaced by Level-4 autonomous line-haul on highway lanes (dock/multi-stop/hazmat work stays human).
labor_tam: $0.5-0.9T [W] confirmed (US heavy-truck driver wage bill; wages/benefits ~43c of every operating dollar at large TL carriers). Note: only ~40% line-haul slice is AV-addressable near-term.
sw_tam: <$100M commercial autonomous-trucking revenue 2026 (pre-scale): Kodiak ~$30M+ recognized but mostly US-military + oilfield, not mass line-haul; Aurora early per-mile/driverless. Per-mile/driver-as-a-service model still forming.
key_players: Aurora (public; 100K+ driverless mi, 2 lanes incl. 600mi FTW-El Paso, target 200+ trucks & observerless kit EOY26; Hirschbach/Werner/Schneider/FedEx/Uber Freight); Kodiak AI (public via SPAC/S-1; 15,600+ revenue loads by Q1-26, driver-out goal EOY26); Waabi (Volvo VNL platform transfer, pre-commercial). Deployment = hundreds of trucks vs ~2M drivers → capture ~0%.
htc_entry_point: None at AV-developer layer — leaders are public/late-stage (Aurora, Kodiak) and capital-intensive; not model-lab, not seed-ownable. Adjacent seed = freight-dispatch voice agents (HappyRobot cross-ref W3.6), autonomous-lane insurance, teleop/remote-supervision.
falsifiable_indicator: Does any operator reach true driver-out (no safety observer) commercial scale >500 trucks by end-2026 (Aurora target 200+; Kodiak driver-out goal EOY26)?
